questions.question: Name a suitable solvent for the potassium hydroxide in the reaction of 1-chlorobutane to form butan-1-ol.
questions.answer: Water (aqueous KOH)
steps: Forming an alcohol is a substitution (hydrolysis) reaction
KOH must be dissolved in water to supply aqueous OH- ions
Ethanol would favour elimination (alkene), so water is the suitable solvent

questions.question: State the type and mechanism of the reaction of 1-chlorobutane with potassium hydroxide.
questions.answer: Nucleophilic substitution by the SN2 mechanism
steps: OH- is a nucleophile that attacks the carbon bonded to Cl
1-chlorobutane is a primary halogenoalkane, so it reacts by SN2 (one step)
Cl- is displaced as the leaving group

questions.question: Draw the mechanism for the reaction of 1-chlorobutane with hydroxide ions, using curly arrows, dipoles and lone pairs.
questions.answer: OH- lone pair attacks the delta+ carbon; C-Cl bond breaks with a curly arrow to Cl; product is butan-1-ol and Cl-
steps: Show the dipole: C is delta+ and Cl is delta- in C-Cl
Curly arrow from a lone pair on O of OH- to the delta+ carbon
Curly arrow from the C-Cl bond to Cl, showing Cl leaving with the bonding pair
Show the product CH3CH2CH2CH2-OH (with H on O) and Cl- with its lone pairs

questions.question: The mass of butan-1-ol formed was 12.1 g and the yield was 64.0%. The density of 1-chlorobutane is 0.886 g cm-3. Calculate the volume of 1-chlorobutane used.
steps: Mr butan-1-ol C4H10O = 74.0; moles = 12.1 / 74.0 = 0.164 mol
Theoretical moles of 1-chlorobutane = 0.164 / 0.640 = 0.255 mol (yield 64.0%)
Mr 1-chlorobutane C4H9Cl = 92.5; mass = 0.255 x 92.5 = 23.6 g

questions.question: What type of reaction occurs when hydrogen peroxide decomposes? A displacement, B disproportionation, C elimination, D hydrolysis.
questions.answer: B (disproportionation)
steps: In 2H2O2 -> 2H2O + O2, oxygen goes from -1 to -2 (reduced) and to 0 (oxidised)
The same element is both oxidised and reduced
This is a disproportionation reaction, answer B

questions.topic: Rate in mol per Second from Gas Volume

steps: Moles O2 per second = 0.50 x 10^-3 / 24 = 2.1 x 10^-5 mol s-1
From 2H2O2 -> O2, H2O2 decomposes twice as fast: 2 x 2.1 x 10^-5 = 4.2 x 10^-5 mol s-1
Answer B

questions.question: State which of 1-chloropropane, 1-bromopropane and 1-iodopropane hydrolyses fastest, and justify the answer.
questions.answer: 1-iodopropane, because the C-I bond is the weakest (lowest bond enthalpy) and iodide is the best leaving group
steps: Bond enthalpy decreases C-Cl > C-Br > C-I
The weakest C-X bond breaks most easily in the substitution step
So 1-iodopropane hydrolyses fastest

questions.topic: Rate of Ammonia with Primary and Tertiary Halides
questions.question: Compare the rate of reaction of ammonia with 1-chlorobutane and with 2-bromo-2-methylpropane, and justify the answer.
questions.answer: 2-bromo-2-methylpropane reacts faster: its C-Br bond is weaker than C-Cl and it forms a stable tertiary carbocation (SN1)
steps: C-Br bond is weaker than C-Cl, so it breaks more easily
2-bromo-2-methylpropane is tertiary and ionises to a stable tertiary carbocation
1-chlorobutane is primary and reacts more slowly by SN2 with a stronger C-Cl bond

questions.question: When 1-chlorobutane is mixed with ethanol and aqueous silver nitrate, which species is the nucleophile? A ethanol, B nitrate ions, C silver ions, D water.
questions.answer: D (water)
steps: The reaction is hydrolysis using the aqueous silver nitrate solution
Water has a lone pair on O and attacks the delta+ carbon
Silver ions are electrophiles (they react with the halide ion), so C is wrong
The answer is D

questions.question: CH3CH2CHBrCH2CH2CH3 is heated with ethanolic potassium hydroxide. How many alkene products are possible (including stereoisomers)? A one, B two, C three, D four.

steps: The compound is 3-bromohexane; H can be lost from C2 or C4
Loss from C2 gives hex-2-ene, which has E and Z isomers
Loss from C4 gives hex-3-ene, which also has E and Z isomers
Total = 4 alkene products

questions.answer: B (the C-Cl bond is stronger than the C-Br bond)
steps: The rate depends on breaking the carbon-halogen bond
The C-Cl bond is stronger than the C-Br bond
A stronger bond breaks more slowly, so the halide is released more slowly
The answer is B

questions.question: Silver nitrate in aqueous ethanol is added to four halogenoalkanes. Which forms a silver halide precipitate in the shortest time? A (CH3)3CI, B (CH3)3CCl, C CH3CH2CH2CH2I, D CH3CH2CH2CH2Cl.

C-I is weaker than C-Cl, so the iodide reacts faster than the chloride
(CH3)3CI is tertiary and has a C-I bond, so it is fastest: A

questions.question: Borax crystals have the percentage composition H 5.2%, B 11.3%, O 71.4%, Na 12.1%. Determine the empirical formula and hence the formula of the borax crystals.

questions.question: Iodine monochloride reacts with propene to form two isomeric products by addition. Draw the skeletal formulae of both isomers.

questions.question: Explain which isomer from the reaction of ICl with propene is the major product.

steps: The I delta+ end of ICl acts as the electrophile and bonds to C1 of propene
This leaves a positive carbocation on C2
C2 is secondary, which is more stable than the primary carbocation alternative (alkyl groups push electron density)
Cl- attacks C2, so the major product is 2-chloro-1-iodopropane

No chlorine atom is oxidised, so the reaction is not a disproportionation (iodine is the species oxidised)

questions.question: If the U-tube is inverted, the yellow solid ICl3 turns to a brown liquid. Explain this observation, using the density of chlorine (about 3 g dm-3) and of air (1.25 g dm-3).

questions.question: Give the formula of the chlorine-containing species present at highest concentration in household bleach at pH 12.
questions.answer: ClO- (chlorate(I) ion)
steps: At pH 12 the solution is strongly alkaline (high OH- concentration)
The equilibrium HClO <=> H+ + ClO- lies far to the right at high pH
So ClO- is the chlorine species at highest concentration

questions.question: Explain why mixing strong acid with bleach is dangerous, justifying the answer using the equilibria.
questions.answer: Added H+ converts ClO- to HClO, then HClO + H+ + Cl- forms toxic Cl2 gas, so chlorine is released
steps: ClO- + H+ <=> HClO (the H+ from the strong acid shifts this equilibrium to the right)
HClO + H+ + Cl- <=> Cl2 + H2O (the Cl- from the acid and H+ push this right)
Toxic chlorine gas is released, which is dangerous

questions.question: On heating, NaClO disproportionates to form sodium chloride and sodium chlorate(V). Give the equation (state symbols not required).
questions.answer: 3NaClO -> 2NaCl + NaClO3
steps: Cl in NaClO is +1; in NaCl it is -1 (reduced); in NaClO3 it is +5 (oxidised)
Three NaClO molecules are needed: two reduced to NaCl, one oxidised to NaClO3
Balanced: 3NaClO -> 2NaCl + NaClO3

A species that donates an electron pair to form a new bond to carbon is a nucleophile

questions.question: Give two reasons why, under the conditions in (b)(ii), the reaction of KOH with 2-iodo-2-methylpropane is faster than with 1-chlorobutane.
questions.answer: The C-I bond is weaker than the C-Cl bond (iodide is a better leaving group); and the tertiary halide forms a stable tertiary carbocation (SN1)
steps: The C-I bond has lower bond enthalpy than C-Cl, so it breaks more easily
Iodide is a better leaving group than chloride
2-iodo-2-methylpropane is tertiary, so it ionises to a stable tertiary carbocation
1-chlorobutane is primary with a stronger C-Cl bond and reacts more slowly

questions.question: Explain the differences in the boiling temperatures of the Group 5 hydrides shown (detailed descriptions of intermolecular forces are not required).
questions.answer: NH3 has the highest boiling temperature because of hydrogen bonding between molecules; for PH3 and AsH3 boiling temperature rises down the group as London forces increase with more electrons
steps: NH3 has N-H bonds with a strongly electronegative N, so it forms hydrogen bonds between molecules
Hydrogen bonds are stronger than other intermolecular forces, so NH3 has the highest boiling temperature
PH3 and AsH3 have no hydrogen bonding and only weak London forces
London forces increase with the number of electrons, so AsH3 boils higher than PH3

questions.question: Explain why hydrogen is a more environmentally friendly fuel than alkanes.
questions.answer: Hydrogen burns to give only water, so it produces no CO2 (greenhouse gas) or other pollutants from carbon, unlike alkanes
steps: 2H2 + O2 -> 2H2O is the only product of hydrogen combustion
Alkanes burn to give CO2, a greenhouse gas that contributes to global warming
Incomplete combustion of alkanes also gives CO and soot (carbon particulates)
So hydrogen is a cleaner fuel

questions.question: Further substitution of ethylamine may occur if the halogenoalkane is in excess. State two features of the ethylamine molecule that make this possible.
questions.answer: Ethylamine has a lone pair on N that makes it a nucleophile, and the electron-donating ethyl group increases the electron density on N
steps: The lone pair on the N atom of ethylamine is still available
So ethylamine acts as a nucleophile and attacks more bromoethane
The ethyl group is electron-donating (inductive effect), making the N more nucleophilic than NH3

A weaker bond breaks faster, so the iodide reacts fastest
The answer is D
